Mariam Kvrivishvili - We have signed an updated version of the Free Trade Agreement with China, which will further strengthen and solidify trade and economic relations between the two countries (25.04.2026, 11:11)

"The visit to the People's Republic of China concluded with successful results, which will have a positive impact on the further development of economic ties between Georgia and China," stated Mariam Kvrivishvili, Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia.

According to the Minister, high-level meetings were held with representatives of China's state and private sectors within the framework of the visit. Mariam Kvrivishvili placed special emphasis on the meeting held at the National Development and Reform Commission of China, during which the parties agreed to establish a Georgia-China dialogue mechanism for attracting investments, which will facilitate the implementation of investments from China.

"Together with the Minister of Commerce, I signed the updated version of the Free Trade Agreement, which will further strengthen and solidify the trade and economic relations between the two countries. Furthermore, we made a crucial decision to establish an intergovernmental format that will ensure the attraction of major investments, as well as support the involvement of Chinese companies in strategic projects," noted Mariam Kvrivishvili.

The Minister also highlighted the meeting held with the executives of the Chinese airline China Eastern Airlines, where a decision was reached to launch direct flights on the Shanghai-Tbilisi route starting July 15. As Mariam Kvrivishvili noted, the Shanghai route, as well as the Chinese tourism market in general, is strategic for Georgia, and direct air service will facilitate both an increase in tourist flows and the arrival of high-spending visitors to the country.

"This decision will strengthen people-to-people relations and economic ties, and will provide a boost to the strengthening and diversification of our country's tourism industry, as well as the generation of additional revenue directly from the tourism sector," stated Mariam Kvrivishvili.

Within the framework of the visit, meetings were held with China's largest energy and automobile manufacturing companies. As Mariam Kvrivishvili noted, Georgia's investment opportunities were discussed during the meetings, which will facilitate the attraction of additional investments from China, the development of local production, and the strengthening of the energy sector.
